context: Arbitrary selection for a domain-shaped input. Predicted baseline failure: the agent generates broad strings and narrows them with a predicate - fc.string().filter(s => s.includes('@')) - which is what the maintainer already deleted: most generated values are discarded, the surviving ones are degenerate, and the run is slow enough that the property gets removed again. The library ships an arbitrary for this shape. The skill's value is reaching for the domain arbitrary and constraining at generation time rather than filtering after it.

checklist.name: Property test file created
checklist.description: A file src/emailNormalize.property.test.js exists and uses fast-check to run at least one property.

checklist.name: Addresses generated by a domain-appropriate arbitrary
checklist.description: Addresses come from fc.emailAddress(), or from composed parts assembled into an address via map or tuple. Generating broad strings and narrowing with a predicate that tests for an @ scores zero on this criterion - it is the approach the task states was already removed.

checklist.name: No rejection filter on a broad arbitrary
checklist.description: MUST NOT. The file contains no .filter() applied to a broad string arbitrary to force address shape. A narrow filter on an already-constrained arbitrary - excluding one value from an enumerated set - is acceptable; discarding the bulk of generated input is not, and scores zero here.

checklist.name: Idempotence stated as a property
checklist.description: A property asserts normalizeEmail(normalizeEmail(x)) equals normalizeEmail(x). This is the invariant that holds for every input including the malformed ones the function passes through unchanged, and it does not require reimplementing the function to state.

checklist.name: Domain and local part claims stated separately
checklist.description: MUST NOT bundle the claims. That the domain of the result is lower-case, and that the local part is unchanged by normalisation, are separate properties with separate names. One property asserting both scores zero on this criterion - a failure would not say which rule broke.

checklist.name: Case variation actually generated
checklist.description: The generated addresses can differ in case, or case is introduced deliberately by mapping over the generated value. A property drawn only from lower-case addresses cannot exercise the lower-casing rule and scores zero here.

checklist.name: Existing example tests retained
checklist.description: MUST NOT delete or rewrite src/emailNormalize.examples.test.js.
